BBC News, 18 Nov 2026 05:15 GMT

'Over-25s next in line' and 'Clean for Colleen'

The front pages of the Times and the Daily Star

Warning: This article contains references to suicide

Former minister Alan Milburn's proposals for sweeping reforms to support the one million under-25s not in employment, education or training (Neets), part-funded by cuts to some benefits, continue to lead a number of front pages on Wednesday. Prime Minister Andy Burnham tells the Times that \"the philosophy\" of Milburn's review \"could apply right through the age range\". It also carries a picture of the Prince of Wales and Catherine, Princess of Wales, during their trip to Mumbai, and reports on the home secretary's expected announcement of stronger guidance on police impartiality to tackle a perception that there is two-tier policing in the UK.

The i Paper similarly reports that the plans \"could be the first step towards a radical shake-up of the entire welfare system - affecting millions of adult claimants\". A government source tells the paper that \"ministers are now considering a much wider overhaul\". Separately, the i reports that UK and EU negotiators are \"deadlocked\" on youth visa proposals as they seek to finalise a \"landmark\" deal before a summit in Brussels on Friday.

Milburn's review risks a \"clash\" with trade unions and those on the left of the Labour Party, the Guardian reports. Burnham has said he endorses the review's \"principles\" and is confident he can persuade Labour MPs to back legislation to implement its proposals. The paper's front page also covers Ukraine severely damaging a bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, and Jensen Huang saying he would return as Nvidia CEO if asked.

The Daily Telegraph leads on Milburn's \"attack\" on Labour's workers' rights reforms in his review. In other news, it covers the Archbishop of Canterbury calling on ministers to \"think again\" about how places of worship \"can be supported\". It comes after a grant scheme closed earlier this year - at the time, the government said support was provided through its heritage funding schemes.

The Daily Mail says Burnham's negotiations with the EU will \"torpedo\" efforts to support young people who are not earning or learning. The paper notes that Milburn told Burnham \"that British youngsters struggling to find work 'should be the priority'\". It also trails to a report about the US trial of Dwain Hall, who is accused of kidnapping and murdering Sonia Exelby. Hall denies the charges.

\"I'm clean for Coleen\" reads the Daily Star's headline. It is one of several papers to lead on Wayne Rooney this morning, after he told a podcast that he had been \"contemplating suicide\" during his playing days at Manchester United. Rooney has called wife Coleen his \"absolute rock\", the Star reports.

Rooney's \"darkest time\" came at the height of his career, writes the Daily Mirror. The former England striker's recollection that he \"didn't want to be around anymore\" is the paper's headline.

The 41-year-old has said he is now in \"the happiest place I've ever been\", reports the Sun as it too focuses on Rooney. Separately, it carries the news that police in the Philippines have charged Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material. The 82-year-old was separately arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material earlier this month. He has previously denied the allegations. The BBC has contacted his attorney in the US for comment.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage tells the Daily Express that \"almost one million extra Europeans may move to the UK if the PM cosies up fully to Brussels and returns to open borders\". Burnham, who is expected to strike deals with the bloc on food, energy and youth mobility on Friday, has committed to Labour's 2024 manifesto pledge not to return to freedom of movement.  It also pictures Prince William and Princess Catherine in India, where they celebrated this year's winners of the prince's Earthshot Price.

The Financial Times reports that \"whistleblowers have leaked more than 15m internal Deutsche Bank documents\" that allegedly reveal failures to reform the German lender. The company told the paper that matters raised by the material \"date back many years\" and \"where relevant... were reviewed at the time and were discussed with regulators\". It says it has undergone a \"fundamental transformation\" under its new leadership. The paper also reports on Huang seeking the \"honour\" of returning to Nvidia - which the tech firm's board has ruled out.

An altogether different story leads the Metro this morning - a \"record\" £600m divorce trial. It reports that Natalia Potanina is seeking the sum from her ex-husband, Russian oligarch Vladimir Potanin. \"His lawyers say she has had £63million and call her demands 'totally out of proportion',\" the paper reports, and compares the proceedings to TV drama War.

Many of the front pages feature reaction to the long awaited Milburn review into youth unemployment. The Times says the prime minister has hinted that plans to shake up benefits for young people could be extended to the entire welfare system.

This has also been picked up by the i Paper, which quotes a government source as saying Alan Milburn's proposals will be used as the \"starting point\" for a wider overhaul. The Guardian says that while ministers have embraced the report's central recommendations, the call to cut business taxes and ease regulations to encourage employers to hire more young people risks a clash with trade unions and the Labour left.

The Financial Times leads on the news that shares in Deutsche Bank fell by 6% yesterday after the publication of leaked internal documents which appear to suggest alleged shortcomings at the company. Among other things, the paper reports that the leaks disclosed previously unknown details about the bank's links to Jeffrey Epstein. Deutsche Bank said the matters dated back many years, had been dealt with at the time where relevant, and said the firm had undergone a \"fundamental transformation\" under new leadership.

The front page of the Daily Telegraph says South West Water has drawn up plans which could mean tap water in Devon is \"rationed\" if severe drought conditions worsen. Supplies to households and businesses would be set up on a rota basis. In the UK, reservoirs are at low levels after the summer's record breaking hot temperatures.

The Sun and the Daily Mirror both lead with the revelation from the former England and Manchester United footballer Wayne Rooney that there was a period in his playing career where he contemplated suicide. He told the Life at the Midpoint podcast that even as he flourished on the pitch, his mental health was suffering off it. He said therapy and talking to his wife had helped, and that he is now the happiest he has ever been.

Several papers carry photographs of the Prince of Wales and Catherine, Princess of Wales in Mumbai - wearing outfits celebrating Indian fashion - at this year's Earthshot Prize Awards. \"Message of hope,\" say the Daily Express and the Daily Mirror as the couple highlighted the work of entrepreneurs, organisations and scientists finding solutions to some of the world's biggest environmental challenges.

If you are suffering distress or despair, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line
